prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. In earlier searches, only one family scored above 0. It feeds the legal-action mask in as input channels under four layouts (as given, transposed, y-flipped, x-flipped) and sums per-type output maps re-laid in those same layouts into the placement logits. This suggests that worlds hide a mismatch between the stated action indexing and the real one. Changes to the recipe, trunk or head alone never helped. Round 1 first reproduces that family faithfully, at a compute ratio near 1 so it keeps the full step budget. Two variants then each change one thing: (a) eight layouts (all dihedral symmetries) instead of four, which covers more possible mismatches; (b) the faithful network trained with 2 PPO epochs, which gives about 1.85 times as many samples. Uniform zeros come from the world, not from seed noise. A nonzero late training success is the first real signal.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored about 0. The best, r1c1, scored 0.002 on one seed and 0.000 on the other, with late training success of 0.0006. That is noise, not a signal. The family that scored in an earlier world does not fit this world under its four layouts or under all eight grid symmetries (r1c2). Doubling the samples with 2 PPO epochs (r1c3) did not help either, which agrees with the earlier finding that recipe-only changes fail. So the action indexing probably differs from the spec in a way that a transpose or flip of the [type, Y, X] layout cannot express. The most likely candidates are type-minor ordering (a = (y*X + x)*T + t, or another order of the three axes) and DONE placed at index 0, which shifts every placement index by one. The network learns the observation and footprints, so channel or type permutations should already be handled. This round tests broader layout hedges. All three use the default recipe so that each result can be read cleanly.

### Round 3
Every trial is effectively 0. The four-layout reproduction (r1c1) built 1 of 512 dev designs on one seed, with late training success of 0.0006. That is within seed noise, but it is the only nonzero signal. Covering more action-index layouts did not help: 8 dihedral layouts, 6 axis orders, DONE-first and 24 order-by-flip layouts all scored 0. So either this world differs somewhere these nets do not cover, or the task is just harder here and needs better learning. Two untested ideas fit: the observation's memory layout may be scrambled (channel-last), so convolutions see noise; or r1c1 lacks capacity and credit for the exact-build bonus. One candidate hedges the observation layout, one deepens the trunk and uses 2 PPO epochs to keep the step budget, and one lengthens the credit horizon. Each extends r1c1, so its result can be compared with r1c1.

### Round 4
Nine trials, and all are at noise level. Only r1c1, the four-layout reproduction, scored at all: 0.002 on one seed, about 1 design in 512, with late training success of 0.0006. The 6-order, DONE-first, 24-layout and channel-last observation hedges all scored exactly 0. A simple re-mapping of action indices is probably not the main problem, or it is not the only one. Recipe changes (2 epochs, gamma 0.99) and a deeper trunk also scored 0. Every difference so far is within seed noise. In this last round I keep the r1c1 family and make three different bets. (1) A head that pools over brick footprints, with corner-anchor hedges, so the net can work out landing layers and whether a brick fits the target. (2) Each observation group (build, target, missing, extra) fed under its own flips and transposes, in case parts of the observation are drawn in different orientations. (3) The same network trained on about 3.25 times more environment samples.

## Trial it ended with
name: Four-layout mask net (reproduction)
hypothesis: A faithful reproduction of the only family that has ever scored. The mask goes in as channels under four layouts (identity, transposed, y-flip, x-flip), plus coordinate channels. A 1x1 stem feeds a residual 3x3 trunk. Per-type logit maps are re-laid in the same four layouts and summed, so the network can learn whichever action indexing the world really uses. Compute ratio is about 1, so it gets the full step budget. If both seeds score 0 on dev, this world's deviation is not one of these four layouts.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: Round 4 proposes "Each observation group (build, target, missing, extra) fed under its own flips and transposes, in case parts of the observation are drawn in different orientations." That points to the right kind of change: the target-related observation channels are spatially misaligned with the build. But it guesses flips or transposes, not a 4-column wrapped shift toward higher x. Round 3's "observation's memory layout may be scrambled" is also vague. The text never states the actual rule.
